arxiv-2106-14233.title: KGRefiner: Knowledge Graph Refinement for Improving Accuracy of Translational Link Prediction Methods
arxiv-2106-14233.creator: Mohammad Javad Saeedizade, Najmeh Torabian & Behrouz Minaei-Bidgoli
arxiv-2106-14233.description: Abstract The Link Prediction is the task of predicting missing relations between entities of the knowledge graph. Recent work in link prediction has attempted to provide a model for increasing link prediction accuracy by using more layers in neural network architecture.

arxiv-2202-12355.title: Symmetric Mass Generation in the 1+1 Dimensional Chiral Fermion 3-4-5-0 Model
arxiv-2202-12355.creator: Meng Zeng, Zheng Zhu, Juven Wang, Yi-Zhuang You
arxiv-2202-12355.description: Abstract Lattice regularization of chiral fermions has been a long-standing problem in physics. In this work, we present the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulation of the 3-4-5-0 model of (1+1)D chiral fermions with an anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetry, which contains two left-moving and two right-moving fermions carrying U(1) charges 3,4 and 5,0, respectively.

arxiv-2209-02689.title: A fast-convolution based space-time Chebyshev spectral method for peridynamic models
arxiv-2209-02689.creator: Luciano Lopez, Sabrina Francesca Pellegrino
arxiv-2209-02689.description: Abstract . Peridynamics is a nonlocal generalization of continuum mechanics theory which adresses discontinuous problems without using partial derivatives and replacing its by an integral operator. As a consequence, it finds applications in the framework of the development and evolution of fractures and damages in elastic materials.

arxiv-2212-14570.title: Spin-1 quarkonia in a rotating frame and their spin contents
arxiv-2212-14570.creator: HyungJoo Kim, Sungtae Cho, Su Houng Lee
arxiv-2212-14570.description: Abstract We propose a new way of studying the spin content of a hadron by looking at its response in a rotating frame. By collecting all responses of quarks and gluons in a rotating frame, we describe the spin-rotation coupling of spin-1 quarkonia and thereby reveal their spin contents in a relativistic formalism.

arxiv-2305-11994.title: ISP meets Deep Learning: A Survey on Deep Learning Methods for Image Signal Processing
arxiv-2305-11994.creator: Matheus Henrique Marques da Silva, Jhessica Victoria Santos da Silva, Rodrigo Reis Arrais, Wladimir Barroso Guedes de Araújo Neto, Leonardo Tadeu Lopes, Guilherme Augusto Bileki, Iago Oliveira Lima, Lucas Borges Rondon, Bruno Melo de Souza, Mayara Costa Regazio, Rodolfo Coelho Dalapicola, Claudio Fi
arxiv-2305-11994.description: Abstract The entire Image Signal Processor (ISP) of a camera relies on several processes to transform the data from the Color Filter Array (CFA) sensor, such as demosaicing, denoising, and enhancement. These processes can be executed either by some hardware or via software.

arxiv-2311-09970.title: Fermi surface symmetric mass generation: a quantum Monte-Carlo study
arxiv-2311-09970.creator: Wei-Xuan Chang, Sibo Guo, Yi-Zhuang You, Zi-Xiang Li
arxiv-2311-09970.description: Abstract The symmetric mass generation (SMG) phase is an insulator in which a single-particle gap is intrinsically opened by the interaction, without involving symmetry spontaneously breaking or topological order. Here, we perform unbiased quantum Monte-Carlo simulation and systematically investigate a bilayer fermionic model hosting Fermi surface SMG in the strongly interacting regime.

arxiv-2401-04564.title: Probing the dipole of the diffuse gamma-ray background
arxiv-2401-04564.creator: A. Kashlinsky, F. Atrio-Barandela, C. S. Shrader
arxiv-2401-04564.description: Abstract We measured the dipole of the diffuse γ \gamma -ray background (DGB) identifying a highly significant time-independent signal coincidental with that of the Pierre Auger UHECR. The DGB dipole is determined from flux maps in narrow energy bands constructed from 13 years of observations by the Large Area Telescope (LAT) of the Fermi satellite.

arxiv-2407-12110.title: Pseudorandomness, symmetry, smoothing: II
arxiv-2407-12110.creator: Harm Derksen, Peter Ivanov, Chin Ho Lee, Emanuele Viola
arxiv-2407-12110.description: Abstract We prove several new results on the Hamming weight of bounded uniform and small-bias distributions. We exhibit bounded-uniform distributions whose weight is anti-concentrated, matching existing concentration inequalities. This construction relies on a recent result in approximation theory due to Erdéyi (Acta Arithmetica 2016).

arxiv-2504-01826.creator: G. Cagareishvili, V. Tsagareishvili, and G. Tutberidze
arxiv-2504-01826.description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigated the Fourier partial sums with respect to general orthonormal systems when the function f f belongs to some differentiable class of functions 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 42C10, 46B07 Key words and phrases: 1.

arxiv-2504-20647.title: Electroactive differential growth and delayed instability in accelerated healing tissues Thanks: Citation : Yafei Wang, Zhanfeng Li, Xingmei Chen, Yun Tan, Fucheng Wang, Yangkun Du, Yunce Zhang, Yipin Su, Fan Xu, Changguo Wang, Weiqiu Chen, Ji Liu, Electroactive differential growth and delayed insta
arxiv-2504-20647.creator: Yafei Wang, Zhanfeng Li, Xingmei Chen, Yun Tan, Fucheng Wang, Yangkun Du, Yunce Zhang, Yipin Su, Fan Xu, Changguo Wang, Weiqiu Chen, Ji Liu
arxiv-2504-20647.description: Abstract Guided by experiments contrasting electrically accelerated recovery with natural healing, this study formulates a model to investigate the importance of electroactive differential growth and morphological changes in tissue repair. It underscores the clinical potential of leveraging electroactive differential growth for improved healing outcomes.

arxiv-2505-16852.title: Coherent states, background fields, and double copy
arxiv-2505-16852.creator: and William Lindved
arxiv-2505-16852.description: Abstract We show that scattering amplitudes on any gauge theory background admitting a coherent state description double copy to amplitudes in a curved spacetime. The metric of the spacetime is built from the gauge background using a notion of classical double copy which emerges naturally at the amplitude level.

arxiv-2511-18314.title: AnyExperts: On-Demand Expert Allocation for Multimodal Language Models with Mixture of Experts
arxiv-2511-18314.creator: Yuting Gao, Lan Wang, Hengyuan Zhao, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu, Qingpei Guo, [0.25cm] AntGroup
arxiv-2511-18314.description: Abstract Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer a promising path toward scalable and efficient large vision-language systems. However, existing approaches rely on rigid routing strategies (typically activating a fixed number of experts per token) ignoring the inherent heterogeneity in semantic importance across modalities. This leads to suboptimal compute allocation, where redundant tokens consume as many resources as critical ones.

arxiv-2511-21307.title: HIRE: A Hybrid Learned Index for Robust and Efficient Performance under Mixed Workloads DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ACM SIGMOD/PODS International Conference on Management of Data; May 31–June 05, 2026; Bengaluru, India ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06
arxiv-2511-21307.creator: Xinyi Zhang, Liang Liang, Anastasia Ailamaki, Jianliang Xu
arxiv-2511-21307.description: Abstract . Indexes are critical for efficient data retrieval and updates in modern databases. Recent advances in machine learning have led to the development of learned indexes, which model the cumulative distribution function of data to predict search positions and accelerate query processing.

arxiv-2512-07869.title: Manifolds and Modules: How Function Develops in a Neural Foundation Model
arxiv-2512-07869.creator: Johannes Bertram, Luciano Dyballa, T. Anderson Keller, Savik Kinger, Steven W. Zucker
arxiv-2512-07869.description: Abstract Foundation models have shown remarkable success in fitting biological visual systems; however, their black-box nature inherently limits their utility for understanding brain function. Here, we peek inside a SOTA foundation model of neural activity ( 54 ) as a physiologist might, characterizing each ‘neuron’ based on its temporal response properties to parametric stimuli.

arxiv-2512-19563.title: On Network-Aware Semantic Communication and Edge-Cloud Collaborative Intelligence Systems
arxiv-2512-19563.creator: Murdadha Nasif, Ahmed Refaey Hussein
arxiv-2512-19563.description: Abstract Semantic communication and edge-cloud collaborative intelligence are increasingly recognized as foundational enablers for next-generation intelligent services operating under stringent bandwidth, latency, and resource constraints. By shifting the communication objective from bit-perfect delivery toward the transmission of task-relevant semantic representations, semantic communication enables adaptive tradeoffs among communication overhead, inference accuracy, computational load, and end-to-end latency.

arxiv-2601-17647.title: Time-Varying Causal Treatment for Quantifying the Causal Effect of Short-Term Variations on Arctic Sea Ice Dynamics
arxiv-2601-17647.creator: Akila Sampath, Vandana P. Janeja, Jianwu Wang
arxiv-2601-17647.description: Abstract Quantifying the causal relationship between ice melt and freshwater distribution is critical, as these complex interactions manifest as regional fluctuations in sea surface height (SSH). Leveraging SSH as a proxy for sea ice dynamics enables improved understanding of the feedback mechanisms driving polar climate change and global sea-level rise.

arxiv-2601-23129.title: Evaluating the Utility of Grounding Documents with Reference-Free LLM-based Metrics
arxiv-2601-23129.creator: Yilun Hua, Giuseppe Castellucci, Peter Schulam, Heba Elfardy, Kevin Small
arxiv-2601-23129.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yilun Hua, Giuseppe Castellucci, Peter Schulam, Heba Elfardy, Kevin Small. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)’s success depends on the utility the LLM derives from the content used for grounding. Quantifying content utility does not have a definitive specification and existing metrics ignore model-specific capabilities and/or rely on costly annotations. In this paper, we propose Grounding Generation Utility ( GroGU ), a model-specific and reference-free metric that defines utility as a function of the downstream LLM’s generation confidence based on entropy.

pmc-10735906.title: EFFECT OF DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AND WORK-RELATED FACTORS ON TRANSITION TO RETIREMENT IN OLDER ADULT
pmc-10735906.creator: Jennifer Saucedo, Jason Newsom, Em Trubits, Mallory Kroeck, Anda Botoseneanu, Heather Allore, Corey Nagel, Ana Quiñones
pmc-10735906.description: Work demands can spillover to family domains (work-to-family conflict; WFC) and family demands may spillover to work domains (family-to-work conflict; FWC). This spillover between domains may help explain the relationship between depressive symptoms and decision to retire among older adults.

pmc-11414994.title: Revolutionizing pharmaceutical innovation: Unveiling the impact of endogenous knowledge spillover in China
pmc-11414994.creator: Zhuolin Li, Lin Guo, Ying Ping
pmc-11414994.description: Modern medical technology innovation is a critical safeguard for human health, while a significant number of developing nations are confronted with the challenge of biopharmaceutical technological advancement. To investigate the possible routes of technological advancement, we investigated the impact of the endogenous knowledge spillover effect on firm innovation endeavors.

pmc-11600962.title: Evidence of a Causal Relationship Between Body Mass Index and Immune-Mediated and Inflammatory Skin Diseases and Biomarkers: A Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11600962.creator: Zhaoyi Li, Yibin Zhao
pmc-11600962.description: AimIncreasing observational studies are revealing a positive correlation between body mass index (BMI) and the risk of Immune-mediated and Inflammatory Skin Diseases (IMID), however the causal relationship is not yet definite.ObjectiveThe aim of the study was to conduct a two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) to explore the potential causality between BMI, and IMID and biomarkers.

pmc-11843271.title: Machine Learning Diagnostic Model for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Based on Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation and Ferroptosis-Related Genes
pmc-11843271.creator: Wenchao Chen, Ting Zhu, Xiaofan Pu, Linlin Zhao, Senhao Zhou, Xin Zhong, Suihan Wang, Tianyu Lin
pmc-11843271.description: Background/Aims:Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a primary liver malignancy with a multifaceted molecular landscape. The interplay between liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) and ferroptosis—a regulated form of cell death—has garnered interest in tumorigenesis. However, the precise role of LLPS and ferroptosis-related genes in HCC progression and prognosis remains obscure. Unraveling this connection could pave the way for innovative diagnosis and therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12527945.title: In-plane dielectric constant and conductivity of confined water
pmc-12527945.creator: R Wang, M Souilamas, A Esfandiar, R Fabregas, S Benaglia, H Nevison-Andrews, Q Yang, J Normansell, P Ares, G Ferrari, A Principi, A K Geim, L Fumagalli
pmc-12527945.description: Water is essential for almost every aspect of life on our planet and, unsurprisingly, its properties have been studied in great detail1. However, disproportionately little remains known about the electrical properties of interfacial and strongly confined water2,3, in which the structure deviates from that of bulk water, becoming distinctly layered4,5.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7151.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7151 — Commissioned officer grades
uslaw-usc-t10-s7151.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7151.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 715 (Appointments In The Regular Army). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The commissioned grades in the Regular Army are: (1) Major general. (2) Brigadier general. (3) Colonel. (4) Lieutenant colonel. (5) Major. (6) Captain. (7) First lieutenant. (8) Second lieutenant.

uslaw-usc-t22-s8005.title: 22 U.S.C. § 8005 — Inoperability of determination and waivers
uslaw-usc-t22-s8005.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s8005.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 87 (United States And India Nuclear Cooperation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A determination and any waiver under section 8003 of this title shall cease to be effective if the President determines that India has detonated a nuclear explosive device after December 18, 2006.
